claim: Lipid droplets (LDs) are cellular organelles specialized for storage of lipids and maintenance of cellular lipid homeostasis.
source: Lipid droplets (LDs) are cellular organelles specialized for storage of lipids and maintenance of cellular lipid homeostasis.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about the function of lipid droplets.

claim: LDs are composed of a neutral lipid core that is covered by a monolayer of phospholipids and other amphiphilic lipids, and by proteins.
source: They are composed of a neutral lipid core that is covered by a monolayer of phospholipids and other amphiphilic lipids, and by proteins (Thiam et al., 2013b; Olzmann and Carvalho, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: LDs vary in size over four orders of magnitude, depending on organism/cell type and fasting state of a cell.
source: LDs vary in size over four orders of magnitude, depending on organism/cell type and fasting state of a cell; in mature adipocytes, the majority of the cell can be occupied by a single LD measuring >100 µm in diameter (Lundquist et al., 2020; Stenkula and Erlanson-Albertsson, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In mature adipocytes, the majority of the cell can be occupied by a single LD measuring >100 µm in diameter.
source: in mature adipocytes, the majority of the cell can be occupied by a single LD measuring >100 µm in diameter (Lundquist et al., 2020; Stenkula and Erlanson-Albertsson, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Secreted lipoprotein particles are similar to LDs in terms of their overall composition but are much smaller, ranging from 10 to 1000 nm in diameter.
source: Secreted lipoprotein particles are similar to LDs in terms of their over-all composition but are much smaller, ranging from 10 to 1000 nm in diameter (Ohsaki et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Proteins can be either stably embedded in the LD monolayer, coming by diffusion from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), from which LDs emerge, or they associate with LDs peripherally from the cytosol.
source: They can be either stably embedded in the LD monolayer, coming by diffusion from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), from which LDs emerge, or they associate with LDs peripherally from the cytosol (Ohsaki et al., 2014; Bersuker and Olzmann, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In mammals, perilipins are a family of five proteins that share related structural features and are highly abundant on LDs.
source: A prominent example is the perilipins: in mammals, this is a family of five proteins that share related structural features and are highly abundant on LDs (Sztalryd and Brasaemle, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Plin2 and Plin3 are widely expressed, whereas Plin1 and Plin4 are most highly expressed in adipocytes, and Plin5 is enriched in oxidative tissues.
source: They vary in their tissue distribution: Plin2 and Plin3 are widely expressed, whereas Plin1 and Plin4 are most highly expressed in adipocytes, and Plin5 is enriched in oxidative tissues (Wolins et al., 2006; Brasaemle et al., 2004; Wolins et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Plin4 and Plin5 are also enriched in muscle tissues.
source: Plin4 and Plin5 are also enriched in muscle tissues.
evidence: This is a statement of fact about tissue distribution of perilipins, likely based on established knowledge.

claim: Plin1 has been shown to regulate the recruitment of lipases to the LD surface.
source: Whereas perilipins contain no known enzymatic motifs, a number of them, in particular Plin1, have been shown to regulate the recruitment of lipases to the LD surface (Sztalryd and Brasaemle, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: All mammalian perilipins contain a predicted AH region in their N-terminal part, which has been shown to be important for their LD localization.
source: All mammalian perilipins contain a predicted AH region in their N-terminal part, which has been shown to be important for their LD localization (McManaman et al., 2003; Nakamura and Fujimoto, 2003; Bulankina et al., 2009; Rowe et al., 2016; Čopič et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The AH region of perilipins is composed of 11-aa repeats that would fold into a 3–11 helix, a slightly extended variant of an α-helix that was characterized in α-synuclein and in apolipoproteins.
source: This region is composed of 11-aa repeats that would fold into a 3–11 helix, a slightly extended variant of an α-helix that was characterized in α-synuclein and in apolipoproteins (Bussell and Eliezer, 2003; Jao et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Both the 11-aa repeat region and the four-helix bundle of perilipins bear structural similarities with apolipoproteins, which are required for formation of lipoprotein particles.
source: Interestingly, both the 11-aa repeat region and the four-helix bundle bear structural similarities with apolipoproteins, which are required for formation of lipoprotein particles (Saito et al., 2003; Melchior et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The 11-aa repeat AH region is by far the longest in Plin4, containing close to 1000 aa in the human protein, with repeats that are highly homologous at the 33-aa level.
source: The 11-aa repeat AH region is by far the longest in Plin4, containing close to 1000 aa in the human protein, with repeats that are highly homologous at the 33-aa level (Čopič et al., 2018; Scherer et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The aa composition of Plin4 AH reveals a striking bias toward small hydrophobic residues, in particular V, T, and A, whereas large residues such as W and F are almost entirely absent.
source: The aa composition of Plin4 AH reveals a striking bias toward small hydrophobic residues, in particular V, T, and A, whereas large residues such as W and F are almost entirely absent (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1A, which shows helical wheel representations of Plin4 AH.

claim: The Plin4 AH region is unfolded in solution, but adopts a highly helical structure in contact with a lipid surface.
source: We have demonstrated that the Plin4 AH region is unfolded in solution, but adopts a highly helical structure in contact with a lipid surface.
evidence: This claim is based on prior work by the authors.

claim: The low hydrophobicity of Plin4 AH promotes specific targeting to LDs, which are permissive for the binding of many amphipathic proteins.
source: The low hydrophobicity of this AH promotes specific targeting to LDs, which are permissive for the binding of many amphipathic proteins (Čopič et al., 2018; Prévost et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The spreading of the phospholipid monolayer on LDs leads to exposure of the hydrophobic core with which the hydrophobic face of an AH can interact more strongly.
source: This is likely due to the physical properties of the LD surface, where the spreading of the phospholipid monolayer leads to exposure of the hydrophobic core with which the hydrophobic face of an AH can interact more strongly (Bacle et al., 2017; Chorlay et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Due to its extreme length, Plin4 in particular can cover a large LD surface and could act as a substitute for phospholipids.
source: Due to its extreme length, Plin4 in particular can cover a large LD surface and could act as a substitute for phospholipids (Čopič et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature and involves speculation about Plin4 function.

claim: A recent study has identified expansion of Plin4 33-aa repeats in a family with a rare autosomal-dominant progressive myopathy.
source: A recent study has identified expansion of Plin4 33-aa repeats in a family with a rare autosomal-dominant progressive myopathy, underscoring the importance of studying this protein (Ruggieri et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Mutations that increased hydrophobicity (T > V) made Plin4 promiscuous for other organelles besides LDs.
source: mutations that increased hydrophobicity (T > V) made Plin4 promiscuous for other organelles besides LDs
evidence: This claim is based on prior work by the authors.

claim: The amphipathic region of Plin4 is capable of emulsifying triolein upon vigorous mechanical mixing (vortex) in aqueous buffer in the absence of any other surfactant, such as phospholipids.
source: The amphipathic region of Plin4 is capable of emulsifying triolein upon vigorous mechanical mixing (vortex) in aqueous buffer in the absence of any other surfactant, such as phospholipids.
evidence: This is a statement of experimental observation from the current study.

claim: A similar result was obtained with a shorter Plin4 AH construct containing 4 33-aa repeats (Plin4 4mer) or a longer construct comprising 12 33-aa repeats (Plin4 12mer).
source: A similar result was obtained with a shorter Plin4 AH construct containing 4 33-aa repeats (Plin4 4mer) or a longer construct comprising 12 33-aa repeats (Plin4 12mer) (Figure 1C; Čopič et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1C and a citation to prior work.

claim: Emulsions of triolein and Plin4 12mer contained spherical oil particles with a large range of sizes; typically with a diameter of 50 to 500 nm (mean ≈ 200 nm), although some larger particles (diameter >1 µm) could also be observed.
source: Electron microscopy and dynamic light scattering (DLS) revealed that emulsions of triolein and Plin4 12mer contained spherical oil particles with a large range of sizes; typically with a diameter of 50 to 500 nm (mean ≈ 200 nm), although some larger particles (diameter >1 µm) could also be observed (Čopič et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: No fluorescence recovery was detected within the time range of the measurement (3 min) when an entire Plin4-oil particle was bleached.
source: As shown in Figure 1D,E, we detected no recovery within the time range of the measurement (3 min).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1D,E showing FRAP experiments.

claim: No fluorescence recovery was observed within 5 min after bleaching a limited area of the lipoparticle surface, neither with Plin4 4mer nor Plin4 12mer.
source: Again, we observed no recovery within 5 min after bleaching, neither with Plin4 4mer nor Plin4 12mer (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1D,E showing FRAP experiments.

claim: Plin4 AH forms a very stable and immobile coat at the surface of triolein.
source: Thus, Plin4 AH forms a very stable and immobile coat at the surface of triolein.
evidence: This is an inference based on the FRAP data showing no recovery.

claim: The emulsions at t = 15 min, 75 min, 4 days and 7 days appeared very similar, showing numerous submicrometer particles and a few larger (>1 µm) particles.
source: As shown in Figure 1F, the emulsions at t = 15 min, 75 min, 4 days and 7 days appeared very similar, showing numerous submicrometer particles and a few larger (>1 µm) particles.
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1F showing microscopy images over time.

claim: Most if not all Plin4 12mer-oil particles remained isolated during this long observation time, showing no obvious clustering or aggregation.
source: Importantly, most if not all particles remained isolated during this long observation time, showing no obvious clustering or aggregation.
evidence: This is an observation from the microscopy data.

claim: The lipoparticles covered by Plin4(4T > S) clustered over time, suggesting that their coat was much less protective than that observed with Plin4 12mer.
source: The lipoparticles covered by Plin4(4T > S) clustered over time, suggesting that their coat was much less protective than that observed with Plin4 12mer (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1F and involves inference about the protective nature of the coat.

claim: Analysis by DLS revealed no change in particle size distribution of Plin4 12mer-oil particles even 28 days after emulsification.
source: Analysis by DLS revealed an even more remarkable stability of Plin4 12mer-oil particles over time, as we detected no change in particle size distribution even 28 days after emulsification (Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1G showing DLS measurements over time.

claim: The stability of Plin4 12mer-oil particles puts Plin4 AH on par with natural emulsifiers used for technological purposes in food or pharmaceutical industry.
source: This puts Plin4 AH on par with natural emulsifiers used for technological purposes in food or pharmaceutical industry (McClements and Gumus, 2016).
evidence: This is a comparison to known emulsifiers, supported by a citation.

claim: The particles formed by Plin4(4T > S) were too heterogenous for analysis by DLS even at the first time-point (3 hr) after emulsion formation.
source: In contrast, the particles formed by Plin4(4T > S) were too heterogenous for analysis by DLS even at the first time-point (3 hr) after emulsion formation.
evidence: This is an observation from the DLS experiments.

claim: After several seconds of introducing Alexa-488-labeled Plin4 12mer into the main channel of the microfluidic system, an increase in fluorescence was detected on the oil interface, which stabilized in ≈ 3 min at a level threefold higher than the fluorescence of the solution.
source: After several seconds, we detected an increase in fluorescence on the oil interface, which stabilized in ≈ 3 min at a level threefold higher than the fluorescence of the solution (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 2C showing time course data from microfluidics.

claim: The fluorescence at the oil interface remained constant after replacing the protein solution in the main channel with buffer, indicating a stable interaction between Plin4 12mer and oil.
source: However, the fluorescence at the interface remained constant, indicating a stable interaction between Plin4 12mer and oil.
evidence: This is an observation from the microfluidics experiments.

claim: No enrichment of fluorescence on the oil interface was observed when buffer containing Alexa488 conjugated to free cysteine was introduced instead of Plin4 12mer.
source: No enrichment of fluorescence on the oil interface was observed when we introduced buffer containing Alexa488 conjugated to free cysteine instead of Plin4 12mer (lower row in Figure 2B,C and Videos 3 and 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 2B,C and Videos 3 and 4.

claim: Plin4 AH forms a very stable protein layer at the oil/water interface.
source: These experiments confirm that Plin4 AH forms a very stable protein layer at the oil/water interface.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the microfluidics experiments.

claim: Fluorescent Plin4 12mer adsorbed to both oil and glass surfaces and even intercalated into the oil-glass interface, making the glass surface visibly heterogeneous.
source: Fluorescent protein also adsorbed to the glass surface and intercalated into the glass-oil interface. The chemically heterogeneous glass surface induced a marked hysteresis in oil-glass contact angle (Joanny and de Gennes, 1984; Figure 2—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Protein adsorption lowered the surface tension of the oil interface.
source: which allowed us to apply the Laplace law and verify that the protein adsorption lowered the surface tension of the oil interface (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1 showing surface tension measurements.

claim: The Plin4(4T > S) mutant assembled on the oil surface with no measurable difference in the kinetics of assembly or in the factor of enrichment compared to Plin4 12mer.
source: The mutant assembled on the oil surface with no measurable difference in the kinetics of assembly or in the factor of enrichment compared to Plin4 12mer.
evidence: This is an observation from the microfluidics experiments comparing Plin4 12mer and 4T>S mutant.

claim: Strong fluorescent signal was observed on the oil interface in the presence of the Plin4(4T > S) mutant at 50:1 molar excess over labeled Plin4 12mer, but not in the presence of Plin4 12mer, indicating that the wild-type protein out-competed with Plin4(4T > S) for oil coating.
source: We observed strong fluorescent signal on the oil interface in the presence of the Plin4(4T > S) mutant, but not in the presence of Plin4 12mer, indicating that the wild-type protein out-competed with Plin4(4T > S) for oil coating (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 2 showing competition experiments.

claim: The number of 11-aa repeats that could be identified in each Plin protein ranged from five for Plin5 to about eight for Plin1/2/3, compared to the 87 repeats in Plin4.
source: The number of 11-aa repeats that we could identify in each Plin protein ranged from five for Plin5 to about eight for Plin1/2/3, compared to the 87 repeats in Plin4.
evidence: This is a statement based on sequence analysis of perilipin proteins.

claim: The repeats are more highly conserved in Plin4, and Plin4 AH is also striking for the absence of any deletions or insertions between the repeats.
source: In addition, the repeats are more highly conserved in Plin4, and Plin4 AH is also striking for the absence of any deletions or insertions between the repeats (Čopič et al., 2018; Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 3A and a citation to prior work.

claim: The 11-aa regions of Plin2/3/4 were similar in character, with low hydrophobicity due to a lack of large hydrophobic residues.
source: Comparison of the composition of the 11-aa regions showed that they were similar in character in Plin2/3/4, with low hydrophobicity due to a lack of large hydrophobic residues (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 3B showing amino acid composition.

claim: Plin1 AH is somewhat more hydrophobic and contains some aromatic residues.
source: Plin1 AH is somewhat more hydrophobic and contains some aromatic residues.
evidence: This is an observation from the amino acid composition analysis.

claim: A more divergent character of Plin1 AH is consistent with the evolutionary divergence of Plin1 from the other perilipins.
source: A more divergent character of this AH is consistent with the evolutionary divergence of Plin1 from the other perilipins (Granneman et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: In wild-type yeast cells, Plin1 AH, but not Plin2 AH, Plin3 AH, or Plin4 4mer, could be observed on LDs.
source: In wild-type cells, Plin1 AH, but not Plin2 AH, Plin3 AH, or Plin4 4mer, could be observed on LDs (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 3C showing localization in yeast cells.

claim: Plin4 6mer and Plin4 12mer localized to LDs in wild-type yeast cells, in line with the finding that increasing the AH length improves LD targeting.
source: In contrast to Plin4 4mer, Plin4 6mer, and Plin4 12mer localized to LDs, in line with our finding that increasing the AH length improves LD targeting (Čopič et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Deletion of Pet10p/Plin1p improved LD targeting of mammalian perilipin constructs, presumably because more LD surface was available.
source: In agreement with the work of Gao et al., deletion of Pet10p/Plin1p improved LD targeting of our mammalian constructs, presumably because more LD surface was available (Kory et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature and involves inference about the mechanism.

claim: Targeting to LDs was further increased by the addition of oleic acid to stationary phase cells, which induced large LDs.
source: Targeting to LDs was further increased by the addition of oleic acid to stationary phase cells, which induced large LDs (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 3C showing localization in yeast cells.

claim: Some perilipin AH protein was observed at the PM, in particular in the case of Plin4 AH, consistent with observations from human cells and tissues.
source: In addition, we observed some protein at the PM, in particular in the case of Plin4 AH, consistent with observations from human cells and tissues (Scherer et al., 1998; Ruggieri et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The 11-aa repeat regions of Plin1, Plin2, Plin3, and Plin4 are all sufficient for targeting LDs.
source: Based on these results, we conclude that the 11-aa repeat regions of Plin1, Plin2, Plin3, and Plin4 are all sufficient for targeting LDs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the yeast localization experiments.

claim: Extrapolating to its full length, Plin4 AH has the highest affinity for LDs, followed by Plin1 AH, and finally by Plin2 AH and Plin3 AH.
source: Comparison of different growth conditions (Figure 3D), and the fact that all Plin AHs were expressed at similar levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), allowed us to establish a ranking of Plin AH-LD affinities. Extrapolating to its full length, Plin4 AH has the highest affinity for LDs, followed by Plin1 AH, and finally by Plin2 AH and Plin3 AH.
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, and involves inference from the data.

claim: Correcting for length differences reveals that per unit of AH length, Plin1 AH has a higher affinity for LDs than AHs of Plin2, Plin3, or Plin4.
source: However, correcting for length differences reveals that per unit of AH length, Plin1 AH has a higher affinity for LDs than AHs of Plin2, Plin3, or Plin4.
evidence: This is an inference based on the localization data and length of the AHs.

claim: The higher affinity of Plin1 AH per unit length is consistent with the higher hydrophobicity of Plin1 AH compared to other perilipin AHs.
source: This is consistent with the higher hydrophobicity of Plin1 AH compared to other perilipin AHs (Figure 3B); higher hydrophobicity has been shown to promote LD binding (Čopič et al., 2018; Prévost et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 3B and citations to prior literature.

claim: LDs were significantly larger (2.5-fold difference in projected area, which would correspond to a fourfold difference in volume) when covered with Plin1, Plin2, or Plin3 AH, compared to LDs covered with Plin4 12mer.
source: Strikingly, we noticed a difference in the size of the LDs that formed in pet10Δ cells grown in oleic-acid-rich medium, depending on the AH expressed (Figure 3C,E): LDs were significantly larger (2.5-fold difference in projected area, which would correspond to a fourfold difference in volume) when covered with Plin1, Plin2, or Plin3 AH, compared to LDs covered with Plin4 12mer (Figure 3C,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 3C,E showing LD size distribution.

claim: LDs with Plin4 6mer were also somewhat larger than those covered with Plin4 12mer.
source: LDs with Plin4 6mer were also somewhat larger than those covered with Plin4 12mer.
evidence: This is an observation from the LD size measurements.

claim: AHs from all four perilipins (Plin1-4) can target LDs and their affinity for LDs correlates with their length and hydrophobicity.
source: We conclude that AHs from all four perilipins (Plin1-4) can target LDs and that their affinity for LDs correlates with their length and hydrophobicity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the yeast localization experiments.

claim: The AH of Plin4 could reduce the size of LDs more strongly than the AHs of other perilipins.
source: However, the AH of Plin4 could reduce the size of LDs more strongly than the AHs of other perilipins.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the LD size measurements.

claim: Plin2 AH-GFP and Plin3 AH-GFP could readily exchange between LD surface and the cytosol in cells grown for 24 hr in oleic acid medium, as reflected by a recovery half-life on the order of a few seconds.
source: Plin2 AH-GFP and Plin3 AH-GFP could readily exchange between LD surface and the cytosol in cells grown for 24 hr in oleic acid medium, as reflected by a recovery half-life on the order of a few seconds (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 4A showing FRAP data.

claim: The exchange of Plin1 AH-GFP was 2–3 times slower than Plin2 AH-GFP and Plin3 AH-GFP, consistent with results obtained in mammalian cells with N-terminal halves of Plin1, Plin2 and Plin3.
source: The exchange of Plin1 AH-GFP was 2–3 times slower, consistent with results obtained in mammalian cells with N-terminal halves of Plin1, Plin2 and Plin3 (Ajjaji et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Plin4 12mer-GFP displayed almost no recovery on LDs over a period of more than 5 min.
source: In striking contrast, Plin4 12mer-GFP displayed almost no recovery on LDs over a period of more than 5 min (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 4A showing FRAP data.

claim: A similar difference between Plin1 AH and Plin4 12mer was observed in cells grown to early stationary phase in standard growth medium.
source: We observed a similar difference between Plin1 AH and Plin4 12mer in cells grown for to early stationary phase in standard growth medium (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 4B showing FRAP data.

claim: Bleaching a small area on the PM in exponentially growing cells showed that Plin4 12mer was highly immobile.
source: Bleaching a small area on the PM in exponentially growing cells showed that Plin4 12mer was highly immobile.
evidence: This is an observation from FRAP experiments on the plasma membrane.

claim: Mobility of Plin4 AH at the PM was increased when shorter constructs (8mer and 6mer) were used, in agreement with the correlation between AH length and binding affinity.
source: Mobility of Plin4 AH at the PM was increased when we used shorter constructs (8mer and 6mer), in agreement with the correlation between AH length and binding affinity (Figure 4D and Čopič et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 4D and a citation to prior work.

claim: Even for the shortest Plin4 AH construct for which LD targeting was consistently observed in yeast membranes, the recovery after photobleaching was at least an order of magnitude slower than for Plin1 AH or Plin3 AH.
source: However, even for the shortest Plin4 AH construct for which we consistently observed targeting to yeast membranes, the recovery after photobleaching was at least an order of magnitude slower than for Plin1 AH or Plin3 AH.
evidence: This is a comparison of FRAP recovery rates.

claim: The particular composition of the Plin4 AH is predominantly responsible for its highly stable interaction with LDs.
source: Given that all AH constructs were expressed at similar levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), that is, the differences in the kinetics were not due to differences in protein concentration, we conclude that, in addition to its length, the particular composition of the Plin4 AH enables its stable binding to LDs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the FRAP data and expression levels.

claim: A large cell-to-cell variability in the FRAP recovery curves of Plin4 12mer-GFP on LDs was observed in Drosophila S2 cells.
source: Interestingly, we observed a large cell-to-cell variability in the FRAP recovery curves of Plin4 12mer-GFP on LDs, whereas in some cells Plin4-12mer on LDs was largely immobile (half-time of recovery >100 s), similar to our results in yeast, in other cells the recovery could be on the order of 1 s (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A; note that within the same cell, the signal on all LDs recovered at the same rate).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1A showing FRAP data in S2 cells.

claim: PC depletion upon CCTα knocked-down had a small effect on Plin4 12mer-GFP FRAP recovery, but this was not the main driver of cell-to-cell variability.
source: PC depletion upon CCTα knocked-down had a small effect, but this was not the main driver of cell-to-cell variability (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1B showing FRAP data after CCT1 knockdown.

claim: A correlation was observed between the rate of FRAP recovery and the intensity of the Plin4 fluorescent signal on LDs.
source: In contrast, we observed a correlation between the rate of FRAP recovery and the intensity of the Plin4 fluorescent signal on LDs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1C showing correlation analysis.

claim: Plin4 AH density at the LD surface influences its dynamics, a feature reminiscent of protein coats.
source: This observation suggests that Plin4 AH density at the LD surface influences its dynamics, a feature reminiscent of protein coats.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between signal intensity and FRAP recovery.

claim: At low membrane coverage level, coat subunits diffuse and exchange quickly; at high membrane coverage level, their polymerization by side-side interaction prevents lateral mobility and fast turnover.
source: At low membrane coverage level, coat subunits diffuse and exchange quickly; at high membrane coverage level, their polymerization by side-side interaction prevents lateral mobility and fast turnover (Saleem et al., 2015; Sorre et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature about protein coats.

claim: Mixing purified Plin3 AH with oil resulted in a highly turbid suspension, similar to the suspensions obtained with Plin4 4mer or Plin4 12mer.
source: Mixing purified Plin3 AH with oil resulted in a highly turbid suspension, similar to the suspensions obtained with Plin4 4mer or Plin4 12mer (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Plin4 4mer-oil droplets displayed a particle size profile with a single peak that did not change over 14 days.
source: By DLS, Plin4 4mer-oil droplets behaved like Plin4 12mer oil droplets (see Figure 1G), displaying a particle size profile with a single peak that did not change over 14 days (Figure 5B, left panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 5B showing DLS measurements.

claim: The droplets produced by Plin3 AH were more heterogenous with larger peak sizes already 3 hr after droplet formation.
source: In contrast, the droplets produced by Plin3 AH were more heterogenous with larger peak sizes already 3 hr after droplet formation.
evidence: This is an observation from DLS measurements.

claim: A spreading of the peaks was observed for Plin3 AH-oil droplets until the samples became too complex for DLS analysis (14 days after formation).
source: Thereafter, we observed a spreading of the peaks until the samples became too complex for DLS analysis (14 days after formation Figure 5B, right panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 5B showing DLS measurements.

claim: Plin3 AH-oil particles were undergoing fusion due to less stable coating by Plin3 AH.
source: Such complexity is generally due to the presence of particles of variable sizes, suggesting that Plin3 AH-oil particles were undergoing fusion due to less stable coating by Plin3 AH.
evidence: This is an inference based on the DLS data.

claim: Folding of Plin3 AH in the presence of the helix-inducing reagent trifluoroethanol (TFE) was similar to what was previously shown for Plin4 AH.
source: We verified using circular dichroism (CD) that this difference was not due to poor folding of the Plin3 helix (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B): folding of Plin3 AH in the presence of the helix-inducing reagent trifluoroethanol (TFE) was similar to what we previously showed for Plin4 AH (Čopič et al., 2018; see also Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1, and a citation to prior work.

claim: A smaller fraction of total Plin3 AH protein was associated with the oil fraction (top of the gradients) than Plin4 4mer or Plin4 12mer.
source: Centrifugation of AH-oil suspensions on sucrose gradients revealed a smaller fraction of total Plin3 AH protein associated with the oil fraction (top of the gradients) than Plin4 4mer or Plin4 12mer (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 5C,D showing sucrose gradient results.

claim: No incorporation of fluorescent Plin4 12mer was observed into preformed Plin4 12mer-oil particles over a period of 24 hr, unless the suspension was vortexed.
source: Consistent with our previous results, we observed no incorporation of fluorescent Plin4 12mer into the preformed Plin4 12mer-oil particles over a period of 24 hr, unless we vortexed the suspension (Figure 5E,F; top panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 5E,F showing protein exchange assays.

claim: Some incorporation of fluorescent Plin4 12mer into Plin4 4mer-oil particles was observed after 3 or 24 hr of incubation, in agreement with a more stable binding of a three-times longer AH.
source: We could observe some incorporation of fluorescent Plin4 12mer into Plin4 4mer-oil particles after 3 or 24 hr of incubation, in agreement with a more stable binding of a three-times longer AH and our cellular data (Figure 5E,F; middle panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 5E,F showing protein exchange assays.

claim: When Plin3 AH was used to pre-form AH-oil particles, Plin4 12mer readily incorporated into these particles, reaching close to maximal particle fluorescence within 10 min after Plin4 12mer addition.
source: In striking contrast, when we pre-formed AH-oil particles using Plin3 AH, Plin4 12mer readily incorporated into these particles, reaching close to maximal particle fluorescence within 10 min after Plin4 12mer addition (Figure 5E,F; bottom panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 5E,F showing protein exchange assays.

claim: Clustering of Plin3 AH-formed oil particles was observed, especially after 24 hr of incubation.
source: In agreement with the DLS data, we also observed clustering of Plin3 AH-formed oil particles, especially after 24 hr of incubation.
evidence: This is an observation from the protein exchange assays.

claim: The specific sequence of Plin4 AH is predominantly responsible for its highly stable interaction with LDs.
source: Because Plin3 AH is only 1.5-times shorter than Plin4 4mer, yet it displays a significantly less stable binding to oil droplets in vitro and to LDs in cells, we conclude that the specific sequence of Plin4 AH is predominantly responsible for its highly stable interaction with LDs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of Plin3 AH and Plin4 AH behavior.

claim: The Plin4 AH sequence displays a remarkable repetitiveness.
source: The Plin4 AH sequence displays a remarkable repetitiveness (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 3A.

claim: Positions of polar and charged residues are extremely conserved among the 33-aa repeats of Plin4 AH.
source: Positions of polar and charged residues are extremely conserved among the 33-aa repeats (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 6A showing a Weblogo plot.

claim: The Plin4 AH sequence shows a strong preference for lysine over arginine (22-fold) and for aspartic over glutamic acid (18-fold).
source: Furthermore, the sequence shows a strong preference for lysine over arginine (22-fold) and for aspartic over glutamic acid (18-fold) (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 3B showing amino acid composition.

claim: Replacing the N[x]6Q sequence with N[x]6N (NN), Q[x]6Q (QQ) or Q[x]6N (QN) almost eliminated the targeting of Plin4 4mer to LDs in HeLa cells.
source: Strikingly, these three mutations almost eliminated the targeting of Plin4 4mer to LDs in HeLa cells (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 6C showing localization in HeLa cells.

claim: The NN 4mer mutant was unfolded in solution but displayed a strong helical signal in the presence of TFE, like Plin4 4mer and Plin4(4T > S).
source: Like Plin4 4mer and Plin4(4T > S), this mutant was unfolded in solution but displayed a strong helical signal in the presence of TFE (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 1 showing CD spectra.

claim: Replacing all aspartates with glutamates (2D > E) led to a small decrease in AH targeting to LDs in HeLa cells.
source: Replacing all aspartates with glutamates (2D > E) led to a small decrease in AH targeting to LDs in HeLa cells
evidence: This is an observation from the localization experiments in HeLa cells.

claim: Replacing the lysine residues with arginine (3K > R) almost abolished AH targeting to LDs.
source: whereas replacing the lysine residues with arginine (3K > R) almost abolished AH targeting to LDs (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 6B,C showing localization in HeLa cells.

claim: A precise interaction between charged and/or polar residues could be important for LD binding.
source: These results suggested that a precise interaction between charged and/or polar residues could be important for LD binding.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mutagenesis results.

claim: The csw 12mer-GFP mutant showed some localization to LDs in HeLa cells, which was significantly reduced compared to Plin4 12mer-GFP.
source: We observed some localization of the longer csw 12mer-GFP mutant to LDs in HeLa cells, which was significantly reduced compared to Plin4 12mer-GFP (Figure 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 6E showing localization in HeLa cells.

claim: The permutations of the sequence in csw 12mer did not affect its helical folding.
source: We verified by CD spectroscopy using purified csw 12mer that the permutations of the sequence did not affect its helical folding (Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A showing CD spectra.

claim: csw 12mer showed a lower ratio of LD-to-PM signal compared to Plin4 12mer in yeast.
source: When we compared the localization of these two constructs in the yeast model, we observed a difference in their distribution between LDs and the PM, with csw 12mer showing a lower ratio of LD-to-PM signal compared to Plin4 12mer (Figure 6G and Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 6G and Figure 6—figure supplement 2B showing localization in yeast.

claim: The preference of csw 12mer for the PM is consistent with the distribution of positive charges in the csw 12mer helix, which is optimal for mediating electrostatic interactions with the negative surface of the PM.
source: This preference for the PM is consistent with the distribution of positive charges in the csw 12mer helix, which is optimal for mediating electrostatic interactions with the negative surface of the PM.
evidence: This is an inference based on the localization data and the charge distribution.

claim: A small shift toward a larger size LDs surrounded by csw 12mer was noted, compared to Plin4 12mer.
source: We also noted a small shift toward a larger size LDs surrounded by csw 12mer, compared to Plin4 12mer (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 2C showing LD size distribution.

claim: The 2T > V mutant exhibited slow recovery curves by FRAP in HeLa cells.
source: Strikingly, whereas 2T > V exhibited slow recovery curves by FRAP in HeLa cells
evidence: This is an observation from FRAP experiments.

claim: The recovery was ~60 times faster for the 2T > V csw mutant compared to 2T > V.
source: the recovery was ~60 times faster for the 2T > V csw mutant (Figure 6H).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 6H showing FRAP data.

claim: Only a precise distribution of charged residues can lead to the exceptional stability that is observed for Plin4 AH at the LD surface.
source: This change in dynamics by two orders of magnitude suggests that if hydrophobicity and electrostatics can roughly compensate for each other to promote effective targeting of AHs to LDs, only a precise distribution of charged residues can lead to the exceptional stability that is observed for Plin4 AH at the LD surface.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the FRAP data comparing 2T>V and 2T>V csw mutants.

claim: csw 12mer could produce oil droplets in the vortexing assay, like Plin4 AH.
source: Like Plin4 AH, csw 12mer could produce oil droplets in our vortexing assay (Figure 7A).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 7A showing turbidity assays.

claim: The droplets formed with csw 12mer were significantly larger by DLS than those formed with Plin4 12mer.
source: However, the droplets formed with csw 12mer were significantly larger by DLS (Figure 7B).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 7B showing DLS measurements.

claim: A significant incorporation of Alexa-488 fluorescence was observed into csw-12mer-oil droplets when Alexa488-labeled Plin4 12mer was added to preformed csw-12mer-oil droplets.
source: When we added Alexa488-labeled Plin4 12mer to preformed csw-12mer-oil droplets, we observed a significant incorporation of Alexa-488 fluorescence into the droplets (Figure 7C,D)
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 7C,D showing protein exchange assays.

claim: Mutations in the polar side of Plin4 AH that reorganized its charged residues led to a large decrease in the stability of Plin4 AH interaction with lipid particles or LDs and a concomitant increase in particle size.
source: Therefore, mutations in the polar side of Plin4 AH that reorganized its charged residues led to a large decrease in the stability of Plin4 AH interaction with lipid particles or LDs and a concomitant increase in particle size, in agreement with our cellular data.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the in vitro and cellular data for csw mutant.

claim: Plin4 12 mer-oil suspensions yielded CD spectra typical of α-helices, with a signature peak at 222 nm.
source: Despite high noise due to the turbidity of the sample, the Plin4 12 mer-oil suspensions yielded spectra typical of α-helices, with a signature peak at 222 nm.
evidence: This is an observation from CD spectroscopy experiments.

claim: The ellipticity signal of Plin4 12 mer-oil suspensions compared well with that of pure Plin4 12 mer solution with TFE within the estimated concentration range.
source: Moreover, the ellipticity signal, which depends on protein concentration, compared well with that of pure Plin4 12 mer solution with TFE within the estimated concentration range (Figure 8A).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 8A showing CD spectra.

claim: On the surface of oil, Plin4 AH folds into a helix, as also observed with the helix-inducing agent TFE or with liposomes containing diphytanoyl phospholipids.
source: These experiments indicate that on the surface of oil, Plin4 AH folds into a helix, as also observed with the helix-inducing agent TFE or with liposomes containing diphytanoyl phospholipids (Čopič et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the CD data and a citation to prior work.

claim: The density of Plin4-12mer on oil was estimated at around 0.07 molecule/nm2, that is, one molecule occupying an area of around 15 nm2.
source: Comparing the surface fluorescence on bead-supported bilayers with surface fluorescence of Plin4-oil particles, we estimated the density of Plin4-12mer on oil at around 0.07 molecule/nm2, that is, one molecule occupying an area of around 15 nm2.
evidence: This is a calculation based on fluorescence measurements on beads and oil droplets.

claim: The estimated density of Plin4-12mer on oil is close to the predicted size of a 3–11 helix 396 aa in length with the structure like the AH of α-synuclein, which would occupy an area of 30 nm2.
source: This is close to the predicted size of a 3–11 helix 396 aa in length with the structure like the AH of α-synuclein (Jao et al., 2008), which would occupy an area of 30 nm2 (0.5 nm x 0.15 nm x 396 aa); therefore, tight packing of such molecules falls within the range of our measurement.
evidence: This is a comparison to a structural model, supported by a citation.

claim: The fluorescence of Plin4 12mer on oil was about 10-fold higher than the fluorescence that could be achieved on bead-supported bilayers at the same fluorescent protein dilution (1:20).
source: We also note that the fluorescence of Plin4 12mer on oil was about 10-fold higher than the fluorescence that we could achieve on bead-supported bilayers at the same fluorescent protein dilution (1:20; see Figure 8B–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 8B–D showing fluorescence measurements.

claim: At higher protein concentrations, the Plin4 AH fluorescence on beads became highly uneven, suggesting formation of domains and distortion of the bilayer.
source: At higher protein concentrations, the Plin4 AH fluorescence on beads became highly uneven, suggesting formation of domains and distortion of the bilayer (Figure 8C, bottom image).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 8C and involves inference about domain formation.

claim: The behavior of Plin4 AH on bead-supported bilayers at high concentrations was reminiscent of the behavior of α-synuclein on liposomes of a similar composition.
source: This was reminiscent of the behavior of α-synuclein on liposomes of a similar composition (Garten et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior work, supported by a citation.

claim: Plin4 AH can achieve a higher density of packing on the surface of neutral lipids than in the presence of phospholipids.
source: We therefore conclude that Plin4 AH can achieve a higher density of packing on the surface of neutral lipids than in the presence of phospholipids.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of fluorescence on oil vs. beads.

claim: Plin4 AH, as well as other perilipin AHs, is unfolded in solution/the cytosol.
source: Plin4 AH, as well as other perilipin AHs, is unfolded in solution/the cytosol.
evidence: This is part of the model summarizing the data.

claim: In contact with a hydrophobic lipid surface, perilipin AHs fold into a helix, whose apolar side engages in hydrophobic interactions with the lipid surface.
source: In contact with a hydrophobic lipid surface, they fold into a helix, whose apolar side engages in hydrophobic interactions with the lipid surface.
evidence: This is part of the model summarizing the data.

claim: Due to the low hydrophobicity of perilipin AHs, their interactions with the lipid surface are weak, and yet sufficient for targeting LDs due to the high length of perilipin AHs.
source: Due to the low hydrophobicity of these AHs, these interactions are weak, and yet sufficient for targeting LDs due to the high length of perilipin AHs.
evidence: This is part of the model summarizing the data.

claim: In the case of Plin4, the helices have a high propensity to interact via polar/charged side-chains, thus forming a highly stable coat on the lipid surface.
source: In the case of Plin4, the helices have a high propensity to interact via polar/charged side-chains, thus forming a highly stable coat on the lipid surface.
evidence: This is part of the model summarizing the data.

claim: Plin4 is a mammalian-specific protein and is highly expressed in adipocytes.
source: Plin4 is a mammalian-specific protein and is highly expressed in adipocytes (Wolins et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Deletion of Plin4 in a mouse model has so far not revealed any strong phenotypes.
source: Its deletion in a mouse model has so far not revealed any strong phenotypes (Chen et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The interaction of Plin4 AH with LDs in vitro and in cellular model systems is remarkably stable.
source: Our experiments show that the interaction of Plin4 AH with LDs in vitro and in cellular model systems is remarkably stable.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings.

claim: The slow lateral diffusion and the very slow dissociation of Plin4 AH molecules at the LD surface as assessed by FRAP, by microfluidics, or by exchange assays, are reminiscent of the behavior of vesicular coat components that polymerize on a membrane surface via lateral interactions.
source: The slow lateral diffusion and the very slow dissociation of Plin4 AH molecules at the LD surface as assessed by FRAP, by microfluidics, or by exchange assays, are reminiscent of the behavior of vesicular coat components that polymerize on a membrane surface via lateral interactions (Saleem et al., 2015; Sorre et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparison to known coat proteins, supported by citations.

claim: The hydrophobicity of perilipin AHs appears at best modest and generally extremely low.
source: Overall, the hydrophobicity of perilipin AHs appears at best modest and generally extremely low.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the amino acid composition analysis.

claim: Perilipin AHs challenge a recent model for AH-LD interaction in which the main driving force is the intercalation of bulky hydrophobic residues within lipid packing defects at the LD surface.
source: As such, these proteins challenge a recent model for AH-LD interaction in which the main driving force is the intercalation of bulky hydrophobic residues within lipid packing defects at the LD surface (Prévost et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement about how the findings relate to prior models, supported by a citation.

claim: The model of bulky hydrophobic residue intercalation does not account for the particular chemistry of Plin AHs, which are the most abundant and specific AHs of LDs.
source: As such, this model does not account for the particular chemistry of Plin AHs, which are the most abundant and specific AHs of LDs.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of prior models.

claim: The polar face of Plin4 AH makes a very large contribution to LD targeting.
source: Surprisingly, the polar face of Plin4 AH makes a very large contribution to LD targeting.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the mutagenesis findings.

claim: Binding of Plin4 AH is controlled by the numerous electrostatic/hydrogen interactions that its polar side chains can engage in along its gigantic length.
source: We thus propose that binding of Plin4 AH is controlled by the numerous electrostatic/hydrogen interactions that its polar side chains can engage in along its gigantic length.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the mutagenesis data.

claim: Numerous Plin4 molecules held together by side-side interactions would form a network at the LD surface.
source: These features speak in favor of a 'coat' model: numerous Plin4 molecules held together by side-side interactions would form a network at the LD surface.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the data.

claim: A prediction of the coat model is that Plin4 should be immobilized at the LD surface and, thereby, should exhibit very limited dynamics.
source: A prediction of this model is that Plin4 should be immobilized at the LD surface and, thereby, should exhibit very limited dynamics.
evidence: This is a prediction from the proposed model.

claim: Plin4 AHs were densely packed on the surface of oil particles, in agreement with the coat model.
source: Furthermore, we showed that Plin4 AHs were densely packed on the surface of oil particles, in agreement with our model.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the density measurements.

claim: Both on LDs in cells and with oil particles formed in vitro, Plin4 AH imposed a smaller size on these structures compared to other perilipin AHs or the csw mutant.
source: Both on LDs in cells and with oil particles formed in vitro, Plin4 AH imposed a smaller size on these structures compared to other perilipin AHs or the csw mutant
evidence: This is a summary statement of the size measurements.

claim: Stable binding of Plin4 AH correlated with smaller LD size.
source: therefore, stable binding of Plin4 AH correlated with smaller LD size.
evidence: This is a correlation observed in the data.

claim: Endogenous Plin4 was observed localizing to small LDs in cultured adipocytes, in contrast to Plin1.
source: Interestingly, endogenous Plin4 was observed localizing to small LDs in cultured adipocytes, in contrast to Plin1 (Wolins et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The coat model of Plin4 is reminiscent of the interactions that apolipoproteins engage in to form secreted lipoprotein particles.
source: The coat model of Plin4 is reminiscent of the interactions that apolipoproteins engage in to form secreted lipoprotein particles (Phillips, 2013).
evidence: This is a comparison to apolipoproteins, supported by a citation.

claim: ApoA1 forms a ring around the lipid core in low-density lipoprotein particles, stabilizing itself via interactions between charged residues from two adjacent molecules.
source: ApoA1, for which most structural information is available, forms a ring around the lipid core in low-density lipoprotein particles, stabilizing itself via interactions between charged residues from two adjacent molecules (Bibow et al., 2017; Pourmousa et al., 2018; Melchior et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Twenty-six intermolecular salt-bridges connect two antiparallel rings of ApoA1, which is about 200 aa long.
source: Twenty-six intermolecular salt-bridges connect two antiparallel rings of ApoA1, which is about 200 aa long.
evidence: This is a statement of fact about ApoA1 structure.

claim: The abundance of positively (3) and negatively (2) charged residues in each 33-aa repeat of Plin4 is compatible with the formation of a similar large network of intra or intermolecular interactions.
source: The abundance of positively (3) and negatively (2) charged residues in each 33-aa repeat of Plin4 is compatible with the formation of a similar large network of intra or intermolecular interactions.
evidence: This is a comparison to ApoA1 and speculation about Plin4 structure.

claim: The coat model of Plin4 does not impose a strict geometry for the protein network.
source: Interestingly, this model does not impose a strict geometry for the protein network.
evidence: This is a statement about the proposed model.

claim: The large number of glycine residues in Plin4 AH (5 G per 33-aa repeat) could enable the formation of various turns, resulting in a spaghetti-like layer rather than a geometrically well-defined assembly.
source: The large number of glycine residues in Plin4 AH (5 G per 33-aa repeat) could enable the formation of various turns, resulting in a spaghetti-like layer rather than a geometrically well-defined assembly.
evidence: This is speculation about the structure of Plin4 on LDs.

claim: The observation that perilipins decorate different LDs in the same cell type supports the model of a higher order perilipin organization.
source: The observation that perilipins decorate different LDs in the same cell type supports our model of a higher order perilipin organization (Hsieh et al., 2012; Wolins et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The network of electrostatic interactions between perilipin AHs should be strongly dependent on their exact sequences, making the formation of hybrid coats with different perilipins less likely than homogenous perilipin coats.
source: The network of electrostatic interactions between perilipin AHs should be strongly dependent on their exact sequences, making the formation of hybrid coats with different perilipins less likely than homogenous perilipin coats.
evidence: This is speculation based on the proposed model.

claim: Non-uniform distribution of Plin1 on LD surface has been observed in cultured adipocytes.
source: Non-uniform distribution of Plin1 on LD surface has been observed in cultured adipocytes (Blanchette-Mackie et al., 1995; Hansen et al., 2017)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Non-uniform distribution of perilipins on LDs can be explained by a coating model, where patches of laterally-interacting perilipin coat might coexist with LD regions decorated by other proteins.
source: this can be explained by a coating model, where patches of laterally-interacting perilipin coat might coexist with LD regions decorated by other proteins.
evidence: This is an explanation based on the proposed model.

claim: A recent study identified an increased number of homologous repeats (10 additional repeats) in the Plin4 AH encoding region of individuals from a single family with a rare muscular degeneration.
source: The sequence of Plin4 is particularly striking in light of a recent study that identified an increased number of homologous repeats (10 additional repeats) in the Plin4 AH encoding region of individuals from a single family with a rare muscular degeneration (Ruggieri et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The study proposes that a higher number of repeats in Plin4 leads to protein aggregation in muscle cells, suggesting that the sequence of Plin4 represents a risk for the organism.
source: The study proposes that a higher number of repeats in Plin4 leads to protein aggregation in muscle cells, suggesting that the sequence of Plin4 represents a risk for the organism.
evidence: This is a statement about a prior study's proposal.
